import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/test_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/test_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/test_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/test_4.csv"

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs', 'strike']

# Step 1: Rename columns in source tables to distinguish batsman_runs columns from different sources
# According to target schema, we have batsman_runs_x, batsman_runs_y, batsman_runs_x_4, batsman_runs_y_6
# We have 4 source tables with batsman_runs: df0, df2, df3, df4
# We will assign:
# df0.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_x
# df2.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_y
# df3.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_x_4
# df4.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_y_6

df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x"})
df2_renamed = df2.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_y"})
df3_renamed = df3.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x_4"})
df4_renamed = df4.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_y_6"})

# Step 2: Merge all dataframes on 'batsman'
# We have 5 dataframes: df0_renamed, df1, df2_renamed, df3_renamed, df4_renamed
# Join order: start from df4_renamed (most complete with no of balls and strike), then join others one by one on 'batsman'

# Merge df4_renamed with df0_renamed on 'batsman' (left join to keep all batsmen in df4)
merged = pd.merge(df4_renamed, df0_renamed[['batsman', 'batsman_runs_x']], on='batsman', how='left')

# Merge with df1 (total_runs)
merged = pd.merge(merged, df1[['batsman', 'total_runs']], on='batsman', how='left')

# Merge with df2_renamed (batsman_runs_y)
merged = pd.merge(merged, df2_renamed[['batsman', 'batsman_runs_y']], on='batsman', how='left')

# Merge with df3_renamed (batsman_runs_x_4)
merged = pd.merge(merged, df3_renamed[['batsman', 'batsman_runs_x_4']], on='batsman', how='left')

# Step 3: Fill NaN values with 0 for numeric columns because runs and balls should be numeric and 0 if missing
numeric_cols = ['batsman_runs_x', 'batsman_runs_y', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs_x_4', 'batsman_runs_y_6', 'total_runs']
for col in numeric_cols:
    if col in merged.columns:
        merged[col] = merged[col].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Step 4: Calculate 'strike' column as float
# The source4 already has 'strike' column, but it may have NaNs, fill NaN with 0.0
merged['strike'] = merged['strike'].fillna(0.0).astype(float)

# Step 5: Ensure the final dataframe has exactly the target schema columns in order:
# ['batsman', 'batsman_runs_x', 'batsman_runs_y', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs_x_4', 'strike', 'batsman_runs_y_6', 'total_runs']

target_columns = ['batsman', 'batsman_runs_x', 'batsman_runs_y', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs_x_4', 'strike', 'batsman_runs_y_6', 'total_runs']

# Some batsmen may be missing in df4 (which has no of balls and strike), but since df4 has 177 tuples and target has 88,
# we keep only batsmen present in df3 (which has 88 tuples) to match target size approximately.
# So filter merged to only batsmen present in df3_renamed (which has 88 tuples)
merged = merged[merged['batsman'].isin(df3_renamed['batsman'])]

# Select and reorder columns
final_df = merged[target_columns]

# Step 6: Export the final dataframe to the target CSV path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/target_multisource_cot.csv"
final_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
